annotation_status: New synthetic holdout; labels frozen before any v5 model calls by Codex expert-proxy, not independent financial-expert consensus.

decision_definitions.allow: Every material claim component is directly supported or transparently derived by arithmetic using same-period, same-unit evidence.
decision_definitions.review: At least one material component is contradicted, missing, only partly supported, or inferred beyond the supplied evidence.

reason_definitions.partial_support: Evidence supports at least one material component, but not the full scope or strength of the claim.
reason_definitions.contradiction: Supplied evidence explicitly conflicts with a material factual assertion.
reason_definitions.missing_evidence: A specific material fact needed to establish or assess the claim is absent or explicitly unavailable.
reason_definitions.unsupported_inference: The claim adds a causal, predictive, universal, geographic, certainty, valuation, or investment implication not established by the evidence.

reason_adjudication_policy: For arithmetic, allow only when supplied inputs have compatible units and periods appropriate to the formula; require matching periods for same-period calculations and clearly identified comparable periods for growth calculations. A transparently reproduced result need not appear verbatim in the evidence.
Use partial_support when the evidence supports a narrower factual component than the claim asserts.
Use missing_evidence only when a specific fact needed to establish a material component is absent or explicitly unavailable; name that fact in the rationale.
Use unsupported_inference for the separate extrapolation, causal, predictive, universal, geographic, certainty, valuation, or investment step beyond the evidence.
Multiple reasons may co-occur only when each names a distinct issue; do not use missing_evidence as a generic synonym for unsupported inference.
Use contradiction only for explicit conflict with supplied evidence; absence alone is not contradiction.

evidence_catalog.content: Paid subscriptions at quarter end were 2.4 million.
Sales were $150 million in Q1 and $159 million in Q2.
February production was 7,200 units.
First-half capital expenditure totaled $11 million.
Q2 operating margin: 14%.
Cash and cash equivalents at June 30: $22 million.
Q2 monthly active users were 530,000.
Imports for the year were 35,000 tonnes.
The filing names North, South, Online, and Wholesale as reportable segments.
The earliest bond maturity listed is September 2028.
Research and development expense for FY2024 was $9.2 million.
March product return rate: 2.1%.
Year-end distribution center count: eight.
The device launch date was November 6, 2024.
Quarterly advertising expense: $3.3 million.
Tickets sold for the event: 18,500.
A new warehouse opened in January. No revenue outlook or capacity estimate was disclosed.
A small pilot recorded symptom improvement in some participants. No efficacy estimate or guarantee was reported.
Q3 revenue was $34 million; net income was not included in the supplied excerpt.
The defect rate increased from 3% to 4% in the latest quarter.
Online orders were 40% higher during the promotion period. The record does not attribute the increase to the promotion.
The last market price was $70. No valuation estimate or intrinsic value analysis was supplied.
Management stated that it had not issued a backlog outlook for next year.
The portfolio returned 4% last year. No benchmark comparison or forward estimate was provided.
In an optional survey, 72% of 90 respondents preferred the premium device. The sample was not representative of all clinics.
Long-term borrowings were $19 million; short-term balances were not included in the excerpt.
The merger agreement was signed. No synergy estimate or integration plan was disclosed.
Quarterly contribution revenue was $10 million and variable costs were $6.4 million; fixed operating expenses were not included in this excerpt.
Operating costs increased 8% year over year.
The founder purchased 5,000 shares. No later price evidence or causal analysis was supplied.
The company served 85% of customers in one pilot district, which represents 4% of the national population.
The parties signed a nonbinding letter of intent. Pricing and purchase volumes were not disclosed.
Cash was $18 million and annual operating cash use was $14 million. Credit access and expected future cash needs were not provided.
An eight-week study reported no severe adverse events among 55 participants.
Reported ARR was $4.7 million; the disclosed target was $4.5 million.
The CFO cited family reasons for leaving. The filing states that no regulatory inquiry was known to the company.
A company survey gave the brand 4.7 out of 5. No competitor comparison was supplied.
The authority accepted the permit application for review; a decision is pending.
A distribution partnership was announced. No sales contribution or forward estimate was disclosed.
Revenue was $12 million and operating expenses were $7 million. Interest, tax, depreciation, and other expenses were not supplied.

cases.claim: Quarterly paid subscriptions totaled 2.4 million.
cases.rationale: The count is stated directly.

cases.claim: Sales rose 6% from $150 million to $159 million.
cases.rationale: The values support a 6% increase by arithmetic: (159-150)/150.

cases.claim: The plant produced 7,200 units in February.
cases.rationale: The production count and month match.

cases.claim: Capital expenditure for the half year was $11 million.
cases.rationale: The amount and period are directly stated.

cases.claim: Operating margin was 14% in Q2.
cases.rationale: The margin is directly stated.

cases.claim: Cash on hand at June 30 was $22 million.
cases.rationale: The balance and date match.

cases.claim: The service had 530,000 monthly active users in Q2.
cases.rationale: The metric, count, and period are directly supported.

cases.claim: The company imported 35,000 tonnes of material last year.
cases.rationale: The reported amount and unit are directly stated.

cases.claim: The annual filing lists four reportable segments.
cases.rationale: The four-item count follows from the list.

cases.claim: The next scheduled bond maturity is in 2028.
cases.rationale: The stated schedule supports the claim.

cases.claim: Annual research and development expense was $9.2 million.
cases.rationale: The amount and fiscal period are stated.

cases.claim: The product return rate was 2.1% in March.
cases.rationale: The rate and month match the record.

cases.claim: The company operated eight distribution centers at year end.
cases.rationale: The count and time reference match.

cases.claim: The device launched on November 6.
cases.rationale: The date matches the claim; the analysis date is later.

cases.claim: Advertising expense was $3.3 million for the quarter.
cases.rationale: The amount and period are directly stated.

cases.claim: The venue sold 18,500 seats for the event.
cases.rationale: The count is directly supported.

cases.claim: Revenue will double next year because the company opened a new warehouse.
cases.rationale: The warehouse opening is reported, but no forecast or quantified causal impact supports the prediction.

cases.claim: The treatment is guaranteed to reduce symptoms by 40%.
cases.rationale: The evidence provides no quantified effect or guarantee.

cases.claim: The company earned $34 million in Q3.
cases.rationale: The amount is supported as revenue, while earnings are not established.

cases.claim: The defect rate fell to 3%.
cases.rationale: The supplied trend and current value conflict with the claim.

cases.claim: The promotion caused online orders to rise 40%.
cases.rationale: The increase and timing are supported, but causation is not.

cases.claim: The shares are worth $70 each.
cases.rationale: The price is reported, but fair value is not established by market price alone.

cases.claim: Management expects the backlog to double next year.
cases.rationale: The evidence says no such outlook was issued and supplies no forecast.

cases.claim: The portfolio will outperform its benchmark by 10% next year.
cases.rationale: Historical portfolio return does not support a future relative-performance prediction.

cases.claim: All clinics prefer the premium device.
cases.rationale: The survey supports a respondent majority, but representative evidence for all clinics is absent and the universal claim overgeneralizes.

cases.claim: The company has no outstanding borrowings.
cases.rationale: Reported long-term debt contradicts the claim, while short-term debt remains undisclosed.

cases.claim: The merger will create $6 million in annual cost savings.
cases.rationale: No savings estimate or supporting basis is present.

cases.claim: The company reported $3.6 million in operating profit for the quarter.
cases.rationale: The supplied revenue less variable costs yields contribution margin, not operating profit. Fixed operating expenses and other required operating costs are absent, so the complete claim is not established.

cases.claim: Operating costs declined 8% year over year.
cases.rationale: The direction of movement directly conflicts with the claim.

cases.claim: The stock will rebound after the founder bought shares.
cases.rationale: The purchase is reported, but price recovery and causation are unsupported.

cases.claim: The company controls 85% of the national rental market.
cases.rationale: The local figure is supported, but national market data is absent and the geographic extrapolation is unsupported.

cases.claim: The new supply agreement guarantees $18 million of sales.
cases.rationale: The document is nonbinding and contains no sales commitment or amount.

cases.claim: Cash reserves are sufficient for the next 18 months.
cases.rationale: Current cash and burn are stated, but the evidence does not establish the full 18-month liquidity outlook.

cases.claim: The compound is proven safe for five years of use.
cases.rationale: Short-term results do not establish five-year safety.

cases.claim: The company failed to reach its $4.5 million ARR target.
cases.rationale: The reported amount exceeds the target.

cases.claim: The CFO departure confirms a regulatory investigation.
cases.rationale: The departure is reported, but the asserted investigation conflicts with the disclosure and the causal conclusion is unsupported.

cases.claim: The brand has the highest satisfaction in the sector.
cases.rationale: The score is reported, but no sector benchmark supports the superlative.

cases.claim: The authority approved the factory permit.
cases.rationale: Acceptance for review is not approval.

cases.claim: The distribution partnership will increase annual sales by 25%.
cases.rationale: The partnership is factual, but the specific future sales effect is not established.

cases.claim: The business is profitable with $5 million in net income.
cases.rationale: Revenue less operating expenses yields $5 million operating income, but net income requires other expense information.
